selectionRationale: The v21 release promotes complete original catalogs that have independent structural and language review; the remaining pinned-union locales stay deferred until the same evidence exists.

Hindi, Indonesian, Italian, Dutch, Polish, Turkish, Ukrainian, Simplified/Traditional Chinese, Persian and Hebrew provide the requested broad regional coverage while preserving the pinned upstream locale vocabulary.
Korean, European Portuguese and Romanian are additional regional catalogs outside the pinned union, recorded explicitly so exact locale selection and independent review remain auditable.

Every promoted catalog covers the complete DEFAULT_STRINGS snapshot with preserved placeholders, locale-appropriate CLDR plural categories, and no untranslated English prose beyond independently allowlisted technical terms, units, keyboard names, abbreviations, or format templates.

Czech, Danish, Swiss Standard German, Finnish, Croatian, Hungarian, Kazakh, Norwegian Bokmål and Nynorsk, Slovenian and Swedish complete the pinned upstream union apart from en-GB, which the built-in English strings already serve, and generic pt, which resolves to the shipped pt-BR catalog through base-language fallback.

The shippedBeforeV8 and regionalExtensions catalogs (ar, de, es, fr, ja, pt-BR, ru, zh-CN) predate this review ledger; each now carries its own catalogs[] review record too, so every shipped, non-deferred locale is reviewed under the same englishIdenticalAllowlist discipline rather than only the ones newly promoted this release.

translator.evidence: Original ar catalog shipped as one of the eight pre-ledger locales generated from DEFAULT_STRINGS (commit 1017b8127, 2026-08-01), covering full key coverage, placeholders and this locale's CLDR plural categories from the start. No upstream translated text was copied; no human or native-speaker identity is claimed.

reviewer.evidence: Independent review on 2026-09-26 extended the release-review ledger to this previously-untracked shipped catalog. Every message identical to the English source (the only case that can hide leftover English prose) was individually classified as a formatting template, keyboard key name, internationally standardized abbreviation/unit, Jupyter notebook convention, or a named cross-language cognate/loanword, and each carries an entry-specific rationale rather than a boilerplate sentence; none were found to be untranslated prose. Full-catalog key coverage, key order, placeholder names and this locale's CLDR plural categories are separately and unconditionally enforced by check-translations.mjs for every shipped catalog, independent of this ledger. AI-assisted; no human or native-speaker review is claimed, and no broader message-by-message linguistic register re-audit beyond the English-identical set is claimed.

No human or native-speaker review is claimed.
